description: Symmetric crypto uses AES-256-CBC (ALGORITHM='aes256') with no authentication tag (no GCM/HMAC), leaving ciphertext malleable and unauthenticated for credential storage.
Encryption key derived via Buffer.from(key,'latin1') with no length enforcement; latin1 decoding shrinks effective keyspace and accepts under-length keys, weakening AES-256 strength.
Production Content-Security-Policy script-src includes 'unsafe-inline' and https:, allowing inline script execution and undermining XSS protection for browsers ignoring strict-dynamic.
Development CSP script-src uses 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https: http:, permitting arbitrary inline and eval'd script execution (XSS sink); see also CWE-79.
CSP style-src allows 'unsafe-inline' for styles, enabling style-based injection and weakening the policy; nonces are not applied to style tags.
API v2 CORS falls back to wildcard origin '*' when ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset in non-production, permitting any origin to call the API in dev/misconfigured deployments.
Cloudflare Turnstile check returns success without validation when CLOUDFLARE_TURNSTILE_SECRET is unset or NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E is set, allowing CAPTCHA bypass; see also CWE-287.
Watchlist blocking check is fail-open: the catch block returns all users as unblocked when the watchlist service errors, allowing blocked users to proceed during outages.
Password policy validPassword() accepts 7-character passwords (rejects only length<7), below the NIST SP 800-63B 8-character minimum, weakening account protection.
isPasswordValid() treats length>=7 as meeting the minimum (admin >14), below the NIST 8-character minimum, permitting weak non-admin passwords.
createWebhookSignature returns an empty string when no subscriber secret is configured, producing unsigned webhook payloads with no integrity/authenticity guarantee.
X-Cal-Signature-256 header is only set when the signature is non-empty, so payloads for secret-less webhooks are dispatched entirely unsigned and unverifiable by subscribers.
Dockerfile bakes default secret ARG NEXTAUTH_SECRET=secret into the build; images built without overriding this ship a predictable, hardcoded auth secret. See also CWE-1188.
Dockerfile bakes default secret ARG CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY=secret; unoverridden builds use a predictable encryption key for AES and JWT signing. See also CWE-1188.
Final 'runner' stage declares no USER directive, so the web container process runs as root, enabling broader impact on container escape or RCE. See also CWE-552.
API v2 Dockerfile declares no USER directive in its only build stage, so the NestJS process runs as root, increasing blast radius of a compromise. See also CWE-552.
CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY is reused as the HS256 JWT signing secret while the same key encrypts data via AES-256-CBC in crypto.ts; cross-protocol key reuse weakens both. See also CWE-328.
SAML Jackson configures its database encryptionKey as CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY, reusing the same secret used for AES encryption and JWT signing across unrelated security contexts.
jwt.verify is called without an algorithms allowlist and with an empty-string secret fallback (CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY||''), enabling algorithm confusion and verification with a blank key.
jwt.verify validates third-party access tokens without specifying an algorithms allowlist, leaving the OAuth token verification open to JWT algorithm confusion.
SAML clientSecretVerifier defaults to the hardcoded value 'dummy' when SAML_CLIENT_SECRET_VERIFIER is unset, an insecure default for verifying OAuth/OIDC client secrets.
SAML Jackson sets idpEnabled:true, enabling IdP-initiated SSO by default, which is more susceptible to login CSRF and unsolicited-response attacks than SP-initiated flows.
getIP trusts client-controllable cf-connecting-ip and x-real-ip headers to derive the client IP used as a rate-limit identifier, allowing spoofing to evade per-IP limits.
forgot-password handler trusts the client-supplied x-forwarded-for header to build the rate-limit identifier, allowing attackers to rotate spoofed IPs and bypass throttling.
Rate limiter is silently disabled (always returns success:true) when UNKEY_ROOT_KEY is unset, removing brute-force/abuse protection on auth and other rate-limited endpoints.
Rate limiter fails open on timeout: the 5s timeout fallback returns success:true, so slow/unreachable limiter backends silently allow unlimited requests.
Rate limiter onError handler fails open by returning success:true, so any limiter backend error disables throttling instead of denying or degrading safely.
Lark webhook verification compares req.body.token to open_verification_token with '===' (non-constant-time), exposing the shared verification secret to timing analysis.
Lark app_ticket handler compares open_verification_token to req.body.token with '===' (non-constant-time), leaking comparison timing for the shared verification secret.
Feishu webhook verification compares req.body.token to open_verification_token with '===' (non-constant-time), exposing the shared verification secret to timing analysis.
Feishu app_ticket handler compares open_verification_token to req.body.token with '===' (non-constant-time), leaking comparison timing for the shared verification secret.
Zoho CRM service logs the OAuth access token via log.debug('Fetched token', this.accessToken), writing a live bearer credential into application logs.
Zoho Bigin service logs the OAuth access token via log.debug('Fetched token', tokenInfo.data.access_token), writing a live bearer credential into application logs.
Lark events handler debug-logs the full request body (log.debug('update token', req.body)) which contains the verification token, risking secret exposure in logs.
Feishu events handler debug-logs the full request body (log.debug('update token', req.body)) which contains the verification token, risking secret exposure in logs.
Environment template ships a concrete default CRON_API_KEY value; deployments copying .env.example unchanged expose a predictable, hardcoded cron API credential.
Environment template sets E2E_TEST_CALCOM_QA_PASSWORD to the weak hardcoded value 'password', a trivially guessable default credential if reused outside test contexts.
